 Naz Reid recorded 14 points (4-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and one block in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Reid has been in a bit of a funk since Charlotte’s October 24 win over the Heat. Over his last four games, the Hornets’ forward has shot 35.1 percent from the field and 21.7 percent from beyond the arc while averaging 12.8 points per game. That’s not the production fantasy managers were hoping for, especially as the Hornets continue to play without Coby White and Kon Knueppel. Hopefully, Reid can turn things around next week, with the Hornets hosting the Pistons on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Naz Reid scored 12 points (5-of-17 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), 11 rebounds, an assist, three steals, and two 3-pointers in 31 minutes. 
 Naz Reid got the start after being benched in the second half of last game, but it looks to be a one game thing. While he didn’t fill up the box score, he still filled up the box score despite it, but it wasn’t a good performance from the Hornets as a whole. If you have Naz, be patient and don’t overreact. He won’t likely go shoot 29.4% from the field and 25% from three very often. 
 Naz Reid 
 CHA 
 Center-Forward 
 #0 
 Naz Reid had seven points (2-of-6 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Pistons. 
 Reid was benched at halftime Wednesday. Hornets coach Charles Lee told reporters after the game that Reid didn’t meet the teams’ standard in the first half and that facilitated the decision to bench him at halftime. Lee didn’t get more specific than that. The move didn’t seem to pay off as the Hornets led by seven at halftime and ended up losing by eight. Fantasy managers with Reid rostered are likely miffed by this whole ordeal, but Lee added that he looks forward to Reid meeting the teams’ standard in the next game, meaning that the benching won’t continue. 
 Naz Reid 
 CHA 
 Center-Forward 
 #0 
 Naz Reid posted a double-double on Monday with 18 points (8-of-22 FGs), 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers against the Wizards. 
 It was a rough start to this game for Reid, and he had just two points on 1-of-3 FGs through three quarters. However, he was incredibly aggressive in the fourth quarter, and it paid off. He had 16 points and seven rebounds in just the fourth quarter, which allowed Charlotte to hang on to the win despite a big fourth quarter from Washington. Reid has gotten off to a strong start to the year for Charlotte and should continue to be a big part of their offense.

 Naz Reid (illness) is probable for Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 Reid popped up on the injury report as probable with an illness, but he’s still likely to suit up against the Wizards Monday. After three games with the Hornets, Reid is averaging 20.0 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 4.0 threes. 
 Naz Reid 
 CHA 
 Center-Forward 
 #0 
 Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday. 
 Reid has been productive in his first season as a Hornet, but this was his highest-scoring performance so far this year. It was also his best field goal percentage and the most triples he’s knocked down in a game this season. Reid has fit in flawlessly with Charlotte’s three-point heavy approach on offense, and he should continue to have some strong scoring nights. Any extra value he can add in other categories will just be a cherry on top.

 Center-Forward 
 #0 
 Naz Reid had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Reid had seven turnovers despite only playing 24 minutes and that’s a crusher in nine-category leagues. Otherwise, he’s scored 37 points on 15-of-34 attempts with seven three-pointers in his first two games with the Hornets. That’ll play. If Reid can keep the turnovers under control, he’s well on his way to paying off his mid-round draft price. 
 Naz Reid 
 CHA

 #0 
 Naz Reid had 20 points (8-of-18 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), 11 rebounds, seven assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s 110-103 victory over the Nets. 
 Reid impressed in his first game with the Hornets. The 27-year-old big man led the team with 20 points, knocked down four three-pointers and was just three assists shy of a triple-double. That’ll play. Reid has never averaged more than 2.2 assists in a season, but the rest of his production is sustainable, making him a valuable player in the middle rounds of fantasy drafts.

 Forward

 Charlotte Hornets start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate in season opener against the Nets 
 The Hornets have Kon Knueppel and Coby White out, so Schroeder and now Sion James will get the start with Grayson Allen coming off the bench. Even in a start, Sion James is not a great per minute producer and will likely not impact many fantasy leagues even in a start. 
 Naz Reid 
 CHA 
 Center-Forward 
 #11 
 Naz Reid tallied 16 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 After scoring 13 points in his Hornets’ preseason debut against the Nets, Reid was a little more effective on Sunday. He shot 50 percent from the field, but the overall stat line was a bit lean. In Charlotte, Reid should have more room to flourish offensively. However, increased usage doesn’t guarantee increased production. His current ADP sits in the middle rounds of 12-team leagues, a fair spot for Reid.

 Kingston Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game against the Pelicans with 3:04 remaining in the fourth quarter. 
 Flemings was ejected after an altercation with New Orleans’ Bryce McGowens. After McGowens blocked Flemings’ layup attempt, the rookie guard threw an elbow at the face of the Pelicans’ wing while play headed in the opposite direction. Multiple players from both teams left their benches, but no one else was ejected because the Hawks had called a timeout. Flemings finished with 12 points, two rebounds, six assists, four steals and one three-pointer.

 Grayson Allen accounted for 27 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and seven three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 After scoring 14 points on 4-of-18 shooting in Charlotte’s prior two games, Allen needed a night like Saturday. He shot a stellar 7-of-10 from beyond the arc, including 3-of-3 in an 11-point first quarter. The 27 points are a new season-high for Allen, who scored 20 or more in two of Charlotte’s first three games. He’ll have a higher fantasy ceiling until Coby White and Kon Knueppel are cleared to return from their injuries.

 Brandon Miller finished Saturday’s loss to the 76ers with 24 points (8-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers.
 Miller shot the ball better than he did in Friday’s loss to the Wizards, when he finished 7-of-24 from the field. This season, he’s shooting 37.7 percent from the field, nearly six percentage points lower than last season (43.5). Hopefully, the eventual returns of Coby White and Kon Knueppel will make things a bit easier for Miller by improving the quality of shots he gets in Charlotte’s offense. The Hornets play three games next week, starting with the Pistons on Monday.

 Edgecombe struggled offensively, but he did make two of his four three-point attempts. Add in the production in some other categories, and this could have been a much worse night for those rostering the 76ers’ guard.  Adem Bona recorded two points (1-of-3 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 With Joel Embiid out, Bona moved into the starting lineup on Saturday. Unfortunately, he produced little, as foul trouble limited him to 22 minutes. Jabari Walker, who played 19 minutes, picked up the slack, finishing with 12 points, six rebounds and one three-pointer. The 76ers don’t have a back-to-back in their four-game Week 3, so Bona’s opportunities are likely to be limited.

 Jaylen Brown (knee) accounted for 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and two steals in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 Back in action after sitting out Friday’s win over the Knicks with left patellar tendinopathy, Brown played 38 minutes against the Hornets. Even with LeBron James and Joel Embiid out, the playing time was somewhat surprising, given the injury Brown was returning from. The good news is that Philadelphia’s schedule for next week doesn’t have a back-to-back. Hopefully, that bodes well for Brown’s availability.
